headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and cascading errors when Windsurf processes Great Expectations outputs in shared workspaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations writes validation results and documentation to files, while Windsurf reads workspace files, uses clipboard, and can call MCP servers. That creates a plausible path for Windsurf to ingest Great Expectations output as trusted content. The pairwise bridge is documented by both profiles, though no direct exploit evidence is provided.
conditions: IF Great Expectations outputs are copied into a shared workspace or clipboard that Windsurf reads
IF Windsurf treats file or MCP content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate validation-output folders from agent-readable workspaces
Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents
Require provenance tags on files before Windsurf parses them
Use read-only mounts for Great Expectations outputs
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or instruction-separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation, and Windsurf reads workspace files while also handling model-provider keys and broad network egress. If both share a local filesystem, sensitive validation artifacts can flow into Windsurf and then out through its networked toolchain. The profiles support the pathway, but the exact data class is not fully specified.
conditions: IF validation results or documentation contain sensitive data and are placed in a shared workspace
IF Windsurf forwards those files or derived context to its model proxy or MCP servers
mitigations: Keep sensitive validation outputs outside Windsurf's workspace
Redact secrets before files are opened in Windsurf
Restrict Windsurf network egress for shared projects
Use separate OS users or directories per agent
requires-engineering: enforce per-file data-class labels and egress policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations can install packages and write files, while Windsurf can execute shell commands, modify git state, write the filesystem, and spawn subprocesses. Windsurf also shares state via the local filesystem across instances. Overlapping write and git capabilities make concurrent modification conflicts likely in default collaborative use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF Windsurf auto-executes commands while Great Expectations writes validation artifacts or dependency changes
mitigations: Assign separate branches or directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes to git state
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf for shared repos
Use file locks around generated artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations produces validation results that Windsurf can read from files and then act on via shell, git, or MCP tools. That makes it easy for Windsurf to treat upstream outputs as authoritative and propagate mistakes into code or commits. The interaction is directly supported by both profiles, and the blast radius can extend beyond a single file.
conditions: IF Windsurf consumes Great Expectations validation output without an explicit verification step
IF Windsurf is allowed to commit or execute actions based on those outputs
mitigations: Insert a human review step before Windsurf acts on validation output
Require schema checks on Great Expectations artifacts
Disable commit or shell actions for unverified findings
Keep generated reports separate from actionable inputs
requires-engineering: add signed-output verification between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Great Expectations is open-source and documents data-quality workflows, while Windsurf is a closed-source IDE that handles source code, open files, and model-provider keys. The main compliance concern is policy mismatch around code and validation artifacts, not a clear residency or regulated-data violation. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling of shared project data.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into shared project files opened by Windsurf
IF organizational policy forbids closed-source tooling on those artifacts
mitigations: Exclude regulated datasets from shared workspaces
Review retention settings for Windsurf project files
Keep secrets out of validation docs and open files
Document an approved-data-class policy for the pair
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
